parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal passport/visa restrictions are traveler-facing and dominate entry: mismatched or X-marker documents can be blocked, confiscated, or deemed material fraud with lifetime ineligibility. Local anti-discrimination law and courts improve private services, street harassment, and student protections, but do not preclude federal screening, government-funded facilities, immigration detention, or corrections practices. If outed, consequences include refusal or stranding, invasive screening, facility exclusion, and severe custody risk where detained; for trans minors, care bans create additional harm. Partial litigation and remedies reduce some local exposure but cannot offset federal operative rules.

entry_documents.exposure: Sex assigned at birth is required for passports/visas; X markers discontinued. Travelers report passports blocked, confiscated, or stranded. Visa officers may refuse cases and pursue material misrepresentation with permanent ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; court challenges, legal-aid FAQs, and foreign travel advisories are documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch triggers secondary review and possible removal or fraud finding; local anti-discrimination law does not alter federal entry screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; national corrections imposes conversion-style policies and birth-sex facility placement for trans people.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Visa, facility, or public-order encounters can escalate into detention; federal custody and corrections authority are not constrained by state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars gender-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; comparable state/province bans include arrest for refusing to depart an opposite-sex public facility.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State/province public-accommodation law covers gender identity, and no division-level bathroom ban or criminal restroom statute is documented for this unit.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protections may work in private settings, but federal facility rules apply to government-funded spaces and can override or out-weigh local law.

care_services.exposure: Adult gender-affirming care friction is not documented, but minors are barred from hormones, puberty blockers, chest surgery and reassignment surgery; federal funding/health rules narrow youth care.
care_services.protection: Grandfather clause for existing youth treatment; state public accommodations cover health care; highest court protects student privacy; sports ban stayed.
care_services.interaction: A travelling trans minor seeking care faces denial, provider discipline, or disclosure; adult trans care risk is uncertain and not a documented entry measure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders rescind trans prison protections, label gender ideology hostile, and counterterrorism language mentions radically pro-transgender groups; multiple foreign advisories cite detentions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime enhancements, anti-panic defence ban, civil-rights enforcement and 88% poll support documented; national hate-crime statute exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat framing raises border/police scrutiny; state law can respond to local harassment but not federal enforcement priorities.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors travelling to this state lose access to gender-affirming care; guardians may be outed at clinics/schools, and national orders criminalize school facilitation of social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: State court protects students; sports ban stayed; anti-bullying covers gender identity; grandfathering preserves some treatment.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian exposure depends on child's status; child's care denial is operative even where local school protections exist and federal entry rules still apply.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National anti-LGBTQ incident census records 72 division incidents without denominator; public majorities support restrictive documents and athletics.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State superior court enforced civil-rights statute against assault; hate-crime enhancements, panic-defence ban and strong pro-protection poll documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street harassment may be addressable locally, but federal entry/custody encounters can bypass state police remedies and place traveller in severe custody.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement varies; several orders are contested, enjoined or blocked; sports-ban status unresolved; incident data lacks denominators; federal facility and custody outcomes for visitors are uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation, legal aid, state civil-rights enforcement and temporary judicial stays are documented and sometimes effective.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may restore care or stop local harm, but short travellers often cannot wait; federal controls remain operative despite state remedies.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both restrict entry documents and deny travel without credible execution; lower here because federal facility rules, visa-fraud ineligibility and severe custody reports exceed routine exclusion/humiliation.
Similar birth-sex custody and facility-arrest risk; somewhat above due state anti-discrimination, court enforcement and no documented local raids, though federal custody keeps it severe/high.
That division protects entry documents, facilities and detention remedies; this jurisdiction lacks protective operative rules at federal level, so score far below.

parsed.synthesis: Federal passport/visa and facility rules dominate: a trans adult alone may be refused entry, stranded or detained if fraud is alleged; detention/custody reports are severe. State anti-discrimination and courts reduce local service and street harm but cannot cancel federal screening, government-funded facilities or corrections. A trans minor’s access to hormones or surgery is barred, adding caregiver/child outing and harm. The combined regime is high-risk, mitigated by litigation and local protections but not by passing or state law.
